more_info.overview: E140 covers chlorophyll extracts and chlorophyllins, which are chemically different preparations of green plant pigments. It is used to add colour or restore colour lost during food manufacture. Chlorophylls are extracted from edible plant material such as grass, alfalfa or nettles. Chlorophyllins are made by treating the extracted pigments with alkali and producing sodium or potassium salts. One specified form is supplied as deep green waxy solid.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; flavoured drinks; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products; unripened cheese excluding products falling in category 16.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.daily_intake: For chlorophylls: ADI classified as not limited (JECFA, 1969). This evaluation does not establish an ADI for every form in the named group.
more_info.origin: Chlorophylls are extracted from edible plant material such as grass, alfalfa or nettles. Chlorophyllins are made by treating the extracted pigments with alkali and producing sodium or potassium salts.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: The specified starting material is plant derived and compatible with vegetarian and vegan diets. The specification does not establish halal or kosher certification.
